text: Which river did Julius Caesar cross in 49 BCE, triggering civil war?

What did Caesar do with the calendar in 46 BCE?

Which office made Caesar chief priest of Rome from 63 BCE onward?
Caesar's comment 'veni, vidi, vici' referred to his swift victory over whom?
At which siege did Caesar decisively defeat Vercingetorix in 52 BCE?
Vercingetorix was a leader of which people?

Who did Caesar name in his will as his adopted son and principal heir?
What was Octavian's birth name before Caesar's adoption transformed his status?
Which Roman magistracy normally came in pairs and stood at the top of the annual cursus honorum?

According to a famous anecdote, Caesar was offered a diadem at the Lupercalia by whom?
The diadem episode mattered because a diadem suggested the status of a what?
Which title did Caesar use repeatedly after victories, emphasizing military success?
Which of these reforms is associated with Caesar's program in Rome?
choices: Permanent division of Italy into themes

text: Caesar increased the size of which governing council, angering some traditional elites?
Which North African king fought against Caesar and died after Thapsus?
What battle in 46 BCE broke major senatorial resistance in Africa?
Which battle in Spain in 45 BCE is usually treated as Caesar's last major military victory?
Caesar's enemies at Munda were largely connected to whose surviving faction?
Which office in the late Republic was supposed to defend plebeian interests and could obstruct legislation?
What phrase is used for Rome's traditional sequence of elite offices?
Which famed orator initially backed Pompey's side but later lived under Caesar's dominance?
Why was Caesar's policy of clementia politically important?
choices: It displayed mercy toward defeated Romans

text: Clementia in Caesar's self-presentation most directly meant what?
Which fellow consul of Caesar in 59 BCE became a byword for political irrelevance that year?
When Caesar crossed the Rubicon, he moved from which province toward Italy?
Which city in Greece hosted the battle of Pharsalus?
Caesar's dictatorship was especially controversial because the office had traditionally been what?
Who was Decimus Brutus in relation to the assassination plot?
Which conspirator shared the name Brutus but was not Marcus Junius Brutus?
Titus Labienus had once served Caesar in Gaul before doing what?
Which legislative assembly was divided by centuries and weighted toward the wealthy?
Which body was formally a council of elders but in practice dominated Roman state policy in the Republic?
What was the immediate political effect of Caesar's assassination?
Which later alliance of Antony, Octavian, and Lepidus emerged from the chaos after Caesar's death?
Which term best describes the Second Triumvirate compared with the First?
What office did Lepidus hold that made him useful in the struggle after Caesar's death?
choices: Master of horse and major military commander

text: Which of Caesar's supporters tried to compromise with the conspirators immediately after the killing?
Whose papers and memoranda became politically explosive after the assassination because they could be used to justify appointments and acts?
Caesar's clemency arguably had what unintended consequence on some enemies?
choices: It sent them into exile forever
It kept potential conspirators alive and influential
It converted them all into allies

text: Which Roman value referred to personal prestige and standing, something Caesar and Pompey both fiercely competed for?
Which Roman value referred to influence derived from reputation rather than formal office?
Why did many aristocrats view Caesar's concentration of offices with alarm?
choices: It threatened the competitive annual magistracies of the Republic
It gave citizenship to slaves immediately
It moved the capital to Alexandria

text: Which office had Caesar held in Spain earlier in his career, giving him military and financial opportunity before the consulship?
The slogan SPQR refers to the Roman people and which other body?
Which of Caesar's victories came after he had already become master of Rome and dealt with resistance in Asia Minor?
Pharnaces II, defeated in the campaign summed up by 'veni, vidi, vici,' was the son of which long-time enemy of Rome?
What was unusual about Caesar's repeated consulships and dictatorship from a republican perspective?
choices: They bypassed the normal rhythm and limits of officeholding
They were illegal because he was not a citizen
They could only apply outside Italy

text: Which Roman writer later portrayed Caesar as both brilliant and destructive in the context of the Republic's collapse?
Caesar's assassination did not save the old Republic largely because it failed to solve what deeper problem?
choices: Concentration of military power in elite hands

text: Which office was traditionally paired with a magister equitum under a dictator?
Who was Caesar's cavalry commander in the traditional dictatorship structure known as the master of horse?
Which province gave Caesar the long command that allowed him to build a personal army and political fortune?
Why was Caesar's army especially loyal to him personally?
choices: He shared campaigns, rewards, and patronage with them

text: Which Roman institution was increasingly undermined when generals like Caesar retained long provincial commands?
What constitutional issue lay behind the showdown over whether Caesar had to return to Rome as a private citizen?
choices: Whether he could keep immunity while standing for office
Whether he could become king of Gaul
Whether he could marry Cleopatra legally

text: Which phrase describes Caesar's attempt to present his autocracy as compatible with republican forms?
choices: Rule through magistracies and honors rather than an open kingship
Rule through hereditary succession already fixed in law
Rule through direct democracy in the assemblies only

text: Which of these men was assassinated before he could become a lasting partner or rival in the post-Caesar order?
What happened at Philippi in 42 BCE that connected directly to Caesar's assassination?
choices: Caesar's killers were defeated by his heirs and allies
The Julian calendar was proclaimed there

text: Which Roman historian wrote Bellum Catilinae and Bellum Jugurthinum and had also been associated with Caesar's camp?
What was the practical significance of Caesar's adoption of Octavian in his will?
choices: It created a powerful dynastic claim in Roman legal form

text: Which festival formed the backdrop to Antony's offering of the diadem to Caesar?
Why did the conspirators miscalculate after killing Caesar?
choices: They had no coherent plan for controlling the state afterward
They forgot to leave the Senate House
They expected Pompey to return from Egypt
They believed the legions would disband at once

text: Which phrase best describes the late Roman Republic during Caesar's rise?
choices: An oligarchic republic under severe strain
A direct democracy with no elite control

text: Which constitutional norm did Caesar violate most dramatically by marching on Rome with troops?
choices: The separation between provincial military command and civic politics in Italy
The ban on winter campaigning in Gaul
The rule that consuls had to be married
The requirement that pontiffs avoid warfare

text: Which statement best captures Caesar's place in Roman history?
choices: He was both a product of republican breakdown and a catalyst of its end
He restored the middle Republic exactly as it had been
He ruled as a legal king recognized by the Senate
He never held military power personally

text: What made Caesar's dictatorship a turning point rather than just another elite rivalry?
choices: It concentrated unprecedented personal power while preserving only the shell of republican institutions
It created the first Roman navy
It ended all civil conflict immediately
It moved the capital to Constantinople

text: Which of these was a public signal that Caesar's honors were pushing beyond normal republican bounds?
choices: Statues, permanent honors, and quasi-monarchical symbolism
The cancellation of all elections forever
The destruction of every temple in Rome

text: In the aftermath of Caesar's rise, what became increasingly clear about the Roman Republic?
choices: Its institutions could no longer reliably contain commanders backed by loyal armies
It had solved the citizenship question permanently in 70 BCE
Its assemblies had become stronger than any individual patron
Its governors no longer sought military glory
